source: NCERT Class IX, Contemporary India I, Geography Ch. 5.

sections.heading: 1. A Biodiversity-Rich Land
points: **Natural vegetation** = plant community growing without human help (virgin/undisturbed).
**Flora** = plants; **Fauna** = animals. India is one of the world's **mega-biodiversity** countries.
Vegetation depends on **relief (land, soil), climate (temperature, photoperiod, precipitation)**.

sections.heading: 2. Types of Natural Vegetation
points: **Tropical Evergreen (Rainforests)** — heavy rain (>200 cm); Western Ghats, NE, Andaman; e.g. rosewood, ebony, mahogany; remain green.
**Tropical Deciduous (Monsoon forests)** — the **most widespread**; shed leaves in the dry season; **teak, sal, sandalwood**.
**Thorn Forests and Scrubs** — arid areas (Rajasthan, Gujarat); **acacia, cactus, khejri, kikar**.
**Montane Forests** — in mountains (change with altitude): oak/pine → deodar/silver fir → alpine grasslands.
**Mangrove (Tidal) Forests** — deltas/coasts; **Sundari trees** (Sundarbans); adapted to salt water.

sections.heading: 3. Wildlife and Conservation
points: India has rich wildlife — tiger (national animal), lion (Gir), elephant, rhino (Kaziranga), peacock (national bird).
Threats: **hunting, habitat loss, pollution**.
Conservation: **national parks, wildlife sanctuaries, biosphere reserves**; projects like **Project Tiger (1973), Project Elephant**.
**18 biosphere reserves**; several are on the **UNESCO** list; a **Botanical Survey** and **Zoological Survey** study flora/fauna.

sections.heading: 4. High-Yield One-Liners (Last-Minute Recall)
points: Vegetation types: tropical evergreen (rainforest), tropical deciduous (most widespread, teak/sal), thorn, montane, mangrove.
Mangrove = Sundari trees (Sundarbans); deciduous forests shed leaves in the dry season.
India = mega-biodiversity country.
Conservation: national parks, sanctuaries, biosphere reserves; Project Tiger (1973).
Vegetation depends on relief, soil, temperature, precipitation.

sections.heading: 5. Common Traps (Watch Out)
points: **Tropical deciduous (monsoon)** forests are the **most widespread**; **teak and sal** are deciduous.
**Mangrove forests** (Sundari trees) grow in **deltas/coastal** tidal areas.
**Tropical evergreen** forests need **very heavy rainfall (>200 cm)**.
**Project Tiger** began in **1973**.
